A remastered collection of an old PS2 RPG series, .hack//G.U. Last Recode is an interesting game that does some things right but also, quite a few things wrong and unfortunately for me these flaws ended up sucking away the enjoyment I had from the game. I will try to explain but please keep in mind that I am completely new to this series, so for old fans and people familliar with the franchise the game will probably be far more enjoyable and worth of your time.

Also an important thing for newcomers: make sure to check the extras, as they include numerous text and video files explaining not only the lore and world of the game, but also the storyline of the previous series (not currently on steam) so you can better dive into Last Recode!

So,
We are introduced to a pretty interesting concept, a "game within a game", taking the role of Haseo, a player of the famous fictional MMO "The World" who, after a series of mysterious and unfortunate events, is on a revenge quest in this virtual world, searching for his nemesis, making friends and enemies along the way.
The game does a marvellous job at immersing you into this concept with the main menu being your "desktop" where you log into the game. There are Forums full of players discussing events and rumors, emails that you can receive and occasionaly exchange discussions, a fanart blog and even browsing through the occasional update of news clips, articles and various other tidbits that explore more of the world (real or virtual) that our hero Haseo lives in. It even has a fully animated web series that updates episodes after you made some progress! The immersion the game offers in this aspect is really one of the most impressive and enjoyable parts of HackGU! 

The visual presentation of the game is also of very high quality with the upscaled graphics and new lighting enhancing the already impressive (for its time) graphics (with cinematic cell shaded cutsenes looking incredible for what is actually a PS2 game) and the same can also be done for the audio department that offers some really great music tracks, from the calm poetic music of the green lush fields, to the ominous choirs of old temples.
having the choice to pick a Japanese dub is always welcome too!

As I mentioned earlier, the story is also quit eengaging and interesting although sometimes a bit convoluted, but despite the problems i have with the actual gameplay (which i will discuss next) i was curious to see how things will turn out in this weird mix of sci-fi and MMO culture. Fair warning though, our protagonist Haseo starts as one of the most extremely unlikeable protagonists i've ever seen in a videogame and his unnecessarily edgy, mean-spirited and childish personality carries for most of the entire 1st part of the trilogy before having a massive improvement during the second part. Thank God!

So it seems that i am gushing for the games presentation and the interesting things it attempts. Then why the negative opinion? Simply put, the horribly repetitive and uninspired gameplay and the way the devs decided to tell the story through it. Full of filler and padding. It's not a case of gameplay "not aging well" - i have no problem playing older or more grindier JRPGs - but even in its time of release back then, i feel this one is not designed very well.

Imagine this:
All three main games in this collection dedicate a large chuck of the story in you advancing through a tournament. 
You log in the MMO. 
Watch a cutscene. 
Clear a dungeon that is the same looking corridor you've seen for the 50th time. (it takes ages to see just a small change/variety in the backgrounds)
Enter the tounrament. Win a round.
Log out to read an email so you can trigger the next story cutscene.
Log in again and clear a filler dungeon so you can progress a short cutscene.
Log out to read an email that tells you to Log in.
Log in and fight a tournamernt round. 
Log out to read an email that tells you to log in.
Log in to enter and finish a filler dungeon so you can again trigger the next round of the tournament/story segment.
Log out to read emails.
Log in to enter the tournament round.
And it' s not just one tournament. Once I became champion during the first part, the 2nd and 3d parts introduce a new one that I need to finish again and again.
Even when there is no tournament, reperat the log in - log out - filler dungeons.

See where this is going? Now multiply this for almost the entirety of three 20hour-each games. 
I was in - what I believe - the middle of the third installment, so close to the end of the main story when I realized I  just couldn't have any more patience for this ordeal when for the 100th time an important character forced me to go with him and spend 30 minutes clearing another random dungeon so he can then decide to talk to me, in a dialog session that barely lasts 1 minute saying stuff that rarely are important to the actual story (sometimes are completely unrelated!) and then forcing me to log out again, read an email AGAIN and repeat the process again...

And it's a shame because underneath all this exhausting filler and repetitive missions they do have a fascinating world to explore but we barely see new locations and surprises along the way. There are plenty of quests and interesting things you can do, like customizing your weapons, riding and customizing a bike, becoming a bounty hunter, things that will give you countlless extra hours of gameplay but all these are part of the same-looking dungeons and worst of all, the difficulty of the game is so unbalanced, you can become so easily powerful, that half of these systems do not matter in the end.

So in the end, perhaps this game is not for me. But from what I can understand, it is a game that caters first and foremost to the fans of the franchise. If you are an old HackGU fan and have any reservation whether this rermaster is good, it is actually really good. The port is fantastic, i haven't encountered bugs and it offers the definitive version of the games, accompanied by tons of extras, (even a parody segment) and most importantly a short but all new 4th chapter that, from what i read, offers a nice epilog.

As a game, I feel it has many flaws that keep it from being very enjoyable and I am not sure I would return to experience it again in the future.

[b]An extremely story-driven JRPG about people playing an MMO, where the worst part about it is the actual game you're playing.[/b]
This consists of 3 HD remasters of the .hack//G.U. games released back in the mid-2000's, and a brand new 4th volume included in this bundle that gives this whole saga a real conclusion.

The story is probably great. It's hard for me to take a plot seriously though when most of everything that happens occurs in the video game within this game. The world outside of the MMO and general lore of this series as a whole is far more interesting and incredibly vast, where the timeline takes place in the futuristic years of the mid-2010's and a lot happens on the outside just because of an MMO.
I think they expected you to have played the previous .hack games and watched the prequel anime though, as they make loads & loads of references to both, and I didn't figure a lot of it out until I watched the backstory videos and searched things up myself.

Ironically, despite the game being about another video game, the gameplay itself is the absolute worst thing about this. It's tedious, repetitious, has loads of pointless mechanics, and so on.
As a JRPG, there's little thought needed into actually playing the game. There are elemental weaknesses, shield breaking, status prevention methods, and all that, but you can go through the whole thing using the same "mash A to kill thing" strategy over & over again while the more complicated-sounding stuff can be completely ignored altogether. The only thing you'll have to worry about is finding equipment with bigger numbers than what you're wearing, but even then you can still get through the story with equipment a hundred levels lower than you so long as your character's level is at the appropriate level for a monster/dungeon; even upgrading said equipment is pointless as stats barely get a boost at all and stronger equipment comes by fast.
The only enemies that can actually give you trouble are the late bosses of each game, but even then you can overcome them fast by doing a quick grind prior to gain a few levels.
I believe they're aware of how terrible the gameplay is in this since they added a "Cheat Mode" to every game that pretty much allows you to breeze through each volume and focus only on the story.

Its storytelling is also pretty obnoxious. Too many times, they want you to log out of the MMO and check your mail to progress the story. Other times they want you to go through a pointless dungeon and/or quest that has absolutely nothing to do with the plot itself, as if all it is is just to pad the time you play.

Each game lasts dozens of hours to go through first-hand if you play them "normally", except for the latest volume which only lasts a few hours and serves pretty much as the epilogue to the whole thing.
In the last volume, they still make you go through practically pointless dungeons even though you no longer need to do much or any leveling by that point, and the gameplay's pretty much the same as the first 3, which is dull.

If you really wanted to just go through the story, you're probably better off watching playthrough videos, or watch the .hack//G.U. Trilogy movie that covers the 3 games and maybe play the short 4th volume yourself.

It is extremely anime, be warned. I picked up the original series when I was a wee lil boy, and I adored them. This time around though, I can't get over how dated the story feels. I remember distinctly thinking the characters looked cool when I was like 10, but the thing is: I'm not 10 anymore. It truly is written in such a way that an edgy pre-teen is meant to identify with these characters (especially Haseo, the main character, good lord he's insufferable). The main character is shit, but somehow there were side characters that annoyed me even more. I'm looking at you, you fat short fucking goofy impersonator. The plot is also kind of predictable, although I will admit a single plot twist got me.

Other than that, the gameplay is extremely dated. It's very hard to get into. Everytime you complete a mission you have to log out and check your in-game email. That's exactly what I want from my JRPG, an email checking simulator. You'd think this is a petty complaint but it really does fuck up the entire flow of the game. They also occasionally make you stop the game and check the online forums for hints and clues for the main plot, which is just as awful as it sounds.

The combat is a little shitty, but you get used to it, and I found myself enjoying it after a while once you get sufficiently overpowered. But even in that regard, the game will sometimes stop you mid-fight during an intense boss to have exposition about how intense the fight that you were LITERALLY just playing is. This is especially bad in volume 1, where near the end every 25% of a boss you cut back to that very boss talking about how much he loves cats or something. Like all anime-esque games, the story is very obtuse like that. The thing that pissed me off the most though is when you spend all this time grinding and then you go to a boss fight, and right as you get their health to zero, the game cuts off and shows you losing the fight because the other person is supposedly too strong. It's extremely frustrating and kind of deflates your hard work.

Anyway, unless you're a weeb, or had a previous connection with the .hack series, I'd recommend not wasting your time.

If you enter an area 10 levels higher than your current level, then you will end up 10 levels higher within 5 minutes. This makes it incredible easy to power level extremely quickly. I never thought I would say this, but the game needs to be more of a grind. If you even look at mobs anywhere near your level, you end up over leveling. If you do sidequests prepare to hit the level cap halfway through any volume.

Nostalgia aside. At some point the story stops being coherent and just becomes a bad attempt at being soulful/artsy thats padded to high hell for time. The sheer amount of pauses, repeated information, cryptic metaphors, unfinished sentences, emotional outbursts that don't fit the situation and just shit thats told instead of shown. By the 3rd volume I just wanted to skip every cutscene, instead I did that for the 4th volume because gross low fps cgi cutscenes that killed any possible redemption.  

Even the game itself is padded for time, between the guild books, and meeting characters in dungeons at the end of the dungeon. The experience is just so off putting that I want to go back and play the first games just to see if its just as shitty or were they on drugs while making GU.

Graphics: Characters look like they're out of some ps2 game. Not abhorrent but not pretty either. I found Gaspard's hands and pies Quad tails the most offensive. The cinematics are nice.

Story: The story starts off well enough, but once it starts talking about a binary virus being able to control people's emotions and damage their physical functions, it becomes too ludicrous to wrap the mind around. I lost interest in the second volume and just wanted to get it over with.

Game play: The Game play is a mind numbing delve. The other reviews were correct in their assessment that it is check Email> Delve into dungeon> Rinse & repeat. Some in an email wants to talk to you? Forget sending you a private message through your personal chat, they just want to tell you the name of who you're facing next at the tournament or they like playing with you at the end of the fourth dungeon floor. Or my favorite-- You're forced by email to go 'level' with your companions in a dungeon that's 20 levels below you just so you can be 'ready' for the fight before they allow you to proceed. Way too much unnecessary time sink filler to bloat a short story. And the gods help you if you're a completionist and achievement hunter like me who is compelled to kill every beast and open every treasure to get that S rank rating at the end.

 I will say that I found the ability to log out and check emails a very nice touch. Would've been better if you could completely log off and walk around or meet some of the girls in rl. Also I liked the Arena PvP fights, but they don't stop letting you fight as much as you like once you reach rank 16 which I think is silly. Should've been able to fight as much you please with practice matches & free for alls.

As for the side quest? They run along the lines of find this creature in 50 different dungeons or defeat these creatures in 100 different dungeons or race your bike in 50 different dungeons. Yeah... NO. Not in those Ps2 style dungeons anyway. Those dungeons would have to be in some immersive 2020 graphics for me to even begin to consider doing that. The Game play is the top factor why I won't be playing with again. Too boring with no Imagination.

Romance: You can marry one of the girls or Endrance in a picture still wedding after the credits. To me an after credits romance defeats the whole purpose of it even being in game. That aside, your character is in high school but can marry an adult woman working for the game company (PI) or a 10 year old girl (Sakubo) in the romance ending. While it is an in-game marriage, the feelings conveyed to their chosen beau are their genuine attraction which implies a real world relationship also being formed. Now keep in mind that the setting is in Japan so whether Haseo is 16 or 17, PI isn't an issue outside American standards. But the 10 year old, Sakubo? That's a totally different and highly inappropriate story that someones child would be online having romantic encounters with a near grown man.

Characters: Not much to say here. Every one of them was a stereotypical anime personality. I will say in particular that I didn't care much for Atoli. She seemed too stupid to exist.

Voice overs: The only good English voice over was Endrance and Sakaki (Alucard from Hellsing). The rest were just unbelievable in their roles. They didn't convey the same emotion for their circumstances in their voices that the Japanese VO did. It sounded like they just got a script and winged it to get the paycheck. 40 year old American women just don't have the capacity to sound like teenage girls.

The Japanese VO were on point. I wish I had them turned on during my first play through. If you want to turn on Japanese Language, you have to do it while you're on the screen to pick a volume. I was ignorant of this and went through the first vol with those horrible English voices.

Characters will say something like "This is just a game." and then 3 minutes later they are completely serious. The writing for the main character is atrocious. [h1][b] TLDR: The pinnacle of mediocrity. Perhaps it was great back in the PS2 days, but the gameplay has not aged well. [/b] [/h1]

[h1]PROS: [/h1]
✅Four games in one package
✅MMO mechanic concepts
✅Great direction, no guide needed unless trying to 100%

[h1]CONS: [/h1]
➖Annoying and repetitive combat
➖Bland and boring game world
➖Constant logging out to check email
➖No cloud saves(!)
➖Excessive hand-holding

Note: This game contains FOUR games. I may refer to games by their volume as follows: 
V1 = Rebirth
V2 = Reminisce
V3 = Redemption
V4 = Reconnection
[h1] [b] Content (Game world/Narrative/Length) – [4/10] [/b] [/h1]
Game World: .hack//G.U. Last Recode (.hack)  imitates the concept of players within an MMO (Massively Multiplayer Online) RPG. Much of the concepts you’ll see in .hack are the same type of concepts that players familiar with MMO games deal with, for example, things like PKing are a core part of the plot and combat in .hack. I do really like the story setting of an MMO game, I feel this opens up a lot of creative possibilities. 

.hack contains two main parts of the game world - the desktop and the game “The World” itself. The desktop is a simple menu containing basic information, like a community forum or your email, something that you’ll be checking a LOT. The World is where the MMO is taking place. This kind of reminds me of something like Final Fantasy XI from a high-level perspective. You visit different areas, kill monsters, and witness a ton of story cutscenes. 

Overall, while I love the creativity, the game world itself is one of the most boring, bland, repetitive, and insufferable worlds I’ve ever trekked through. As of this review I have only finished V2 and still often visit level 90 zones that are the same exact look and feel of the level 10 zones. It's just so painful going to the repeat zones, with zero exciting things other than the usual monsters/chests over and over and over again. 

Narrative: There is a heavy focus on the story for .hack games. It's a big part of the overall package. Again, the concepts of a story setting in an MMO sounds very intriguing to me - players that are killed in game are ending up in comas in real life! Unfortunately, I found articles in EVE Online that were more thrilling than anything .hack has. 

I think a part of it is the repetition. In both V1 and V2, a core part of the story is the boring arena. When I learned I have to slog through the arena all over again, I rolled my eyes and audibly said no. 
Another part of it is the exaggeration. I get that this is a universe where technology has advanced and the game is played with something more advanced than a monitor. But every time a character died, all I could think of is Randy dying in the World of Warcraft South Park episode with how serious .hack characters refer to PVP. 

The last part is just the anime tropes. The early 2000s were a different era, and of course .hack is an anime and was before it was a game, but it really just feels like I’m playing an anime instead of a video game based on an anime. Like no real humans would act or talk in this way. Like one of those PR video game trailers where they include the live comms of multiplayer matches. Like you know players aren’t like that, if that makes sense. 

Length: The entire package is very long. Expect to take ~20-25 hours on each of the 3 main title entries with much less for the 4th extra content. Even more so when you factor in side content, quests, and endgame min/maxing. 

[h1][b] Gameplay (Mechanics/Difficulty) – [4/10] [/b] [/h1]
Mechanics: The core of the gameplay, and what you’ll spend the majority of the time doing when you’re not in a cutscene, is combat. I found the combat to be simple, repetitive, and boring, only barely picking up halfway into V2. 

V1 you will literally mash the attack button 95% of the time, with the remaining time being the occasional block or the weapon skill for the Rengeki combo. There’s barely any sort of progression or customization with weapons or gear, you only have 3 slots to equip. You gain nothing on level up but I guess more HP/Attack/Defense. The few weapon skills you have are unexciting to use and just do damage but mainly serve as the only reason for your existence - Rengeki combos. And your AI companions are dumb as bricks and would die without you holding their hand through everything. 

I will end by saying if all this isn’t bad enough, the combat is plain frustrating, especially in V2 as you progress. See, enemies will eventually start to CC you with things like sleep or paralyze, so you get the joy of watching your idiot companions attempt to kill things while you are CC’d for 15 seconds. OR enemies will hit you with an attack, knock you back, and constantly float you if you miss time a block. One of my most hated elements of any game is when you take control away from the player, and this game does it CONSTANTLY. It's so fun charging up your weapons attacks only for an enemy to sneeze on you and interrupt everything. 

Difficulty: Incredibly easy. The only time you’ll ever have any trouble is if you intentionally go to an area that is much higher level than you, but apparently the games EXP values have been adjusted to where grinding isn’t necessary anymore. 

[h1] [b] Graphics (Quality/Performance) – [4/10] [/b] [/h1]
Quality: Kinda bad. Graphics look like a slightly more HD PS2 game. Reminds me of a less detailed Final Fantasy X. I’d say by far the worst part graphically of the game is the areas and all the copy pasted, low-res assets that just repeat endlessly. 

Performance: Good, almost no issues at all with the game, I only experienced a single crash on V2. Otherwise, .hack kept a solid 60fps with no dips. 
i9-13900KF | RTX 4090 | 64GB RAM | 1440p @ 240hz | installed on SSD

[h1] [b] Audio (Sound Effects/Music) – [5/10] [/b] [/h1]
Sound Effects: Good enough. English voice acting is very good, apart from some characters like Endrance and his moaning whispery voice (Sorry Liam, much <3). 

Music: Not bad, but largely forgettable, this is no Final Fantasy where the music is top notch. 

[h1] [b] Replay Factor (Longevity) – [2/10] [/b] [/h1]
There is some good amount of side content to play through, and achievements, but I have no idea why you’d want to replay through the .hack games again other than nostalgia. 

[h1] [b] Final Verdict – [5/10] [/b] [/h1]
.hack is one of the most easily mediocre games I’ve ever played. It's just so bland, so boring, and a trial in patience. I wish the single player MMO game actually felt like an MMO, which is one of my favorite genres. 

The best part about buying .hack//G.U. Last Recode is the amount of content that you get. Even if I didn’t enjoy the games myself, you should consider a purchase when on sale due to having the most complete collection of .hack that is ever and might ever be on PC. I think I bought this game for ~$10 on sale and the amount of content you get for $10 is crazy, well over 60 hours, if you can stomach through the parts that didn’t age well. 

For me, I’m going to take a break after V2 and take a long hard consideration before I start V3, if ever, so consider this my review for the game, otherwise, I’ll edit it in the future.

This isn't just a review of G.U. but also the entire .hack franchise.

I would absolutely not recommend .hack at all, but I will admit the idea of it is very interesting. I don't think a whole lot can really be done with the whole "game within a game" setup, but the real plot of the franchise is actually pretty cool. That being magic died a long time ago, but its slowly coming back through technology, specifically its starting to manifest using MMOs as its pathway, in particular the MMORPG known as "The World".

The issue is that this plot is done in probably the most uninteresting way possible. The OG series takes so long to get through only for a whole lot of nothing to happen. The anime bored me out of my mind and I can't remember anything of plot relevance happening aside from the ending. The "games" (really just one game with four seperate discs lets be honest here) were awful too, I couldn't even make it past the first one because I think it might be one of the crappiest RPGs I've ever played. Watched a playthrough of the rest and it takes forever for interesting plot moments to happen, and even then they are so short lived. Its a whole lot of nothing really.

G.U. is an improvement over the OG series, credit where credit is due but it still falls short of what I would recommend. I will admit I did not fully beat G.U. but I did make it past volume 2. I kept trying to convince myself to finish up the post-game content for v2 or to move on to v3 but whenever I considered it I just had this voice in the back of my head keep saying "There are loads of other great RPGs that you could play instead when this game is only a 5/10 even in its best moments." The two biggest praises I can give G.U. are 1: that the story has much better pacing and it feels like things are actually happening at a slow, but fast enough pace to keep my interest. Once again the anime was a whole lot of nothing though. 2: The combat is infinitely better than the combat in the OG series, alas it is not good enough to convince me to beat this series but there is real potential and room to expand it into an actually great combat system should Bamco ever decide to revive this franchise.

I think there is real potential in the series, and I would be interested in a reboot or something but the series that we currently have lacks a story solid enough to be memorable and lacks any truly fun gameplay.

I'm a fan of the dot hack series (be it games, animes or light novels) and I still have the PS2 version of those games but let's be honest, this remaster is a joke ... potentially a scam.

Let's skip the fact that a playstation controller isn't supported despite the game being originally from PS2 and now only on playstation 4, and that the game hasn't an option for playstation overlay buttons. It's a inconvenience (most of all for the tightly timed QTE when disarming traps) but can be worked around with mods.

No the real problem is the lack of work this port ... or should I say ... this emulation has receive.
- saves that disappear magically after some random period of time (edit : they are actually still there but you need to restart Steam -not just the game- to see them again) (edit2 : launching the game with administrator's rights seem to prevent that to happen ... seriously bad port).
- Many visual glitches (edit: most -but not all- can be worked around by setting the shadows to low).
- Lack of proper PC options, and some of them aren't properly implemented, like for vsync where enabling it locks the game at 30 fps ... but with the game being slow down since the speed is tied to the framerate, or disabling vsync which locks at 60 fps but with a tearing fest like you probably never seen. (edit: the vsync 30fps lock only seems to apply when using full screen mode. You can use borderless windows to work around that but have to use the same resolution as your desktop).
- PC options not even accessible in-game. You have to return to the title screen (the one where you can select which game to load) but you can't even quit the game unless you spend 30 minutes in the 1st part of the tutorial (but you usually want to test the settings right of the bat).
- Same (very short) draw distance as on PS2.
- Textures barely upgraded on the background (it's ok on the characters) which is very (very) blurry. (edit: texture filtering is indeed doing more harm than anything, disabling it got you less blurry textures).
- And so on.

Add to that, that the game isn't an especially good Action RPG if you're not into dot hack storyline. The gameplay is quite limited, the game ask the player to "return IRL" quite frequently ("guess I will log out and check my emails" will be the sentence you will hear the most), the ctuscene using the game engine are strange since there is a delay before each character started talking which results in something quite funny when the conversation heating up but is plagued with silence between each sentence), which would be unthinkable nowadays, but since they didn't even port the game correctly, it's no use to expect they would refine the game itself.

Frankly I really hesitated to ask for a refund right away. The only reason I didn't was because, as I said, I'm a fan and having already finished that game on PS2, I want to know what is the 4th story/game they added.

For those that are still interested in the game, I would strongly recommend to get it on console.

Having played many MMOs since when Ultima Online was the latest and greatest MMORPG, it was very interesting to play a game that centered around a "simulated MMORPG".  This game gets the simulated MMORPG aspect down very well in my opinion, with incredible detail-orientation to the Operating System, Online Jack, and related forums to make you feel like it's a fully contained "real" world that takes place 15 years in the future (which is now two years ago roughly in actual time, haha...it's interesting how much they got right).  

Unfortunately, I can't say the same about the story, which is REALLY unfortunate given this game's reputation.  The protagonist that you play is extremely tough to like until Volume 3 perhaps, which is primarily why I don't care for the game's story.  The one positive thing I can say about the story is that it is very approachable and not drawn out.  Except for Volume 4 (which is really Volume 3.5), each volume is roughly 20 - 25 hours in length.  Volume 4 is only 4 hours in length at most...thus the Volume 3.5 designation.

The gameplay is a little off-balance.  I didn't have to use any magic spells until Volume 2, and then it was sparingly, as one example.  Magic almost feels like an afterthought.  I don't get why they included the bike.  Sure there was some activities there, but it was not a fully fleshed out idea in my opinion.  

I can't say that I recommend, regardless of it's "modern classic" status according to some.

The very dated low effort trilogy from CyberConnect2.

The good:
I really can't think of any part of this game I thought was well done

The bad:
The side quests are terrible and easily missed.
The scaling changes to the game make it far too easy to outlevel things if you try and do most of the content.
This is a remaster?  How???  Except for brief 5 second scenes that use updated character models, everything is just using the ancient ugly models from the original.

The ugly:
The writing blows, I don't know if this is a poor translation or what but both the dialogue and the story suck.
The voice acting for many characters is like nails on a chalkboard.
There is so little variety - the game takes place almost entirely in randomly generated dungeons, but there are only 4 tilesets for these dungeons and each of them only have 2-3 rooms each.
The combat is terrible - you spam attack until a purple circle pops up, then you push R1.  That is the whoooole combat.

Thoughts:
CyberConnect2 makes bad games.  I really really regret giving them a chance and buying this.  There is so little effort put into this game that it is shocking.

Combat is simply spamming your attack button until you see a purple circle on an enemy, then using any ability on that enemy.  The game calls this a "RENGEKI" and gives you bonus XP and damage for doing it.  The game acts like this is a big deal.

Combat takes place in one of 4 places that the game makes procedural dungeons out of.  Calling them procedural or randomly generated feels like a joke, as it is the most barebones and basic generation I have ever seen.  Each of the 4 places only has a couple of rooms, and the game just connects them together in random directions.  These are not interesting rooms, they are all squares that can have exits on each of their 4 sides, or hallways leading to the next square.  Sometimes you see a trap room ala Phantasy Star Online, but these 'trap rooms' are terrible and you can always just walk around the outside of the traps and to the next room.

Side quests come from a side quest vendor, not by meeting people.  If you don't remember to check the side quest vendor, you will quickly outlevel the few quests he offers (I believe this is due to the levelling being sped up for this 'remaster').

The writing is impossible to get invested in.  Characters in the game treat the MMO as if it is life or death, and it gets old within seconds.  The game acts like PvP is a huge morally grey decision, and spends an absurd amount of time talking about it.  I was hoping for a game that featured the types of people you meet in MMOs and told an actual story, but this feels like a weird impression of how a 5 year old would view an MMO.

I wish there was some part of this game I could say I liked, or that I could recommend it to some group of people, but this is intolerable trash that I really wouldn't wish on anyone.

Verdict.
Ignore this and any other CyberConnect2 games, they only care about their visuals.

Short Version: DON'T BUY unless you're a masochist with too much free time, I don't know what other reviewers smoked but it had to be good stuff to get this pseudo-game to "Very Positive" rating.

Long Version:
Gameplay: MMO-like but fights are a chore, exploration is mindless, no character customization, the list goes on, I tried giving the game a chance but it never opened up.

Story: have you ever watched a generic shounen anime? the tropes are all here, edgy main character, goofy sidekicks, mysterious ally, overpowered villains, etc..

Sound: Decent soundtrack, nothing to complain effect wise; the english voice acting is atrocious, I'm not experiencing the japanese one and I can still feel they're butchering the little humanity the characters have.

Graphics: Everything is okay for the year these originally came out, the main cast looks awful I must say, the art style isn't gorgeous but I saw some decent looking models running around the world/dungeons, too bad you can't play/recruit them.

Final Note: honestly, when I buy an oldschool jrpg I dont expect to be amazed, I've played too many for that too happen, this game stung though, because, not only is its gameplay especially tedious, but also it sets up a whole mmorpg world and system that absolutely feels underused and explored, it sits you down in a multicoloured sand box and tells you you can only do castles and only in one specific colour: sure, you can extract some fun out of that, but it quickly dries out and you can't help but wonder all the stuff you could attempt to create were you not hindered by those early rules; if, like me, this is your first contact with the series, I'd advise you to skip this one and find some other sandbox to enjoy yourself in.
